verdict.rationale: Snowflake documents core primitives for background automation — Snowpipe continuous ingestion, Streams for change capture, GA Dynamic Tables that auto-refresh, and resource/anomaly monitors that autonomously suspend warehouses or alert on cost — plus a headless CLI (`snow sql`) that can be scripted/cron'd for autonomous execution. However there is no evidence of an AI-agent-specific scheduler or orchestration layer that lets an AI-native user set up an agent to run continuously/autonomously in the background; the Cortex Agents MCP server is described as an on-demand retrieval interface, not a background automation trigger. Missing for 10: explicit AI-agent scheduling/orchestration framework, autonomous multi-step agent workflows, and independent/hands-on confirmation that these primitives are actually used to run unattended AI automations.
